1._section_summary: This abstract reports a single online study of 646 British community adults (447 women) aged 18–76 who completed the MAIA, Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2), and other body-image measures. Hierarchical regressions showed MAIA subscales predicted multiple facets of body image after controlling for sex, BMI, and age, with the exception of the MAIA Body Listening subscale. The section does not report mean age, mean BMI, participants' race/ethnicity, education levels, BMI assessment method, or Pearson correlations between BAS-2 and BMI.
